title: Navimower 0.4.2-beta7

Navimower 0.4.2-beta7 adds regional routing for the private mobile-app cloud and an evidence-first mower capability profile. The official Smart Home OAuth/MQTT branch remains separate and keeps using broker information supplied by the official API.

### Regional private-cloud routing

Private-cloud setup no longer assumes that every Navimow account belongs to the European/FRA passport service. Before sending the account password, Navimower now asks the known regional passport directories with the signed `GET /v3/region` request and resolves the account to Europe (`fra`/`eu`), Asia-Pacific (`sg`/`sea`), Americas (`us`/`ore`) or mainland China (`bj`).

After passport authentication the client probes the bounded mower-cloud host candidates for that region, retains the first usable host and persists the resolved hostname into the Home Assistant config entry after a successful private-cloud refresh. Existing European entries continue to select the same FRA hosts. The observed US `ore` account routing keeps `navimow-fra.ninebot.com` first because a working H210 diagnostics capture confirmed that combination.

The region lookup sends only the account address and the standard device marker. If a regional directory cannot be checked, setup fails closed instead of sending the password to a guessed server.

### Smart Home MQTT remains independent

This change does not derive Smart Home OAuth/API routing or the MQTT broker from the private-cloud region. Navimower still requests official MQTT credentials through the Smart Home API and uses the returned `mqttHost` / `mqttUrl` connection details. This keeps the two vendor transports independent instead of assuming that their regional topology is identical.

### Evidence-first capability profile

A sanitized capability profile is now attached to parsed mower snapshots and Home Assistant Download diagnostics. It records:

- whether important private-cloud endpoint payloads are present, empty or missing;
- setting key paths reported by the mower, without copying setting values into the capability inventory;
- positively observed capability groups such as schedule, map/zones, coverage, maintenance, position, cutting height, weather, lighting, VisionFence/navigation, terrain and anti-theft settings;
- narrow known model constraints, currently including the proven lack of user-defined ordered zone mowing on first-generation H-series mowers.

Positive observations remain sticky for the lifetime of the loaded coordinator. A missing or empty response is deliberately **not** interpreted as proof that a feature is unsupported. This beta does not prune the general sensor platform; it establishes the evidence model needed to make future entity provisioning safer across H, i and X families.

### Diagnostics and architecture

Download diagnostics now includes `private_cloud_region` and `capabilities` sections in addition to the existing sanitized raw snapshot. The architecture document and permanent runtime guard were updated for the new responsibility-based modules; no beta-numbered production runtime layer was reintroduced.

Regional host discovery and the observed US routing are aligned with the field-tested work published by `ilguala/navimow_pro`. Navimower keeps its own Smart Home MQTT branch and its existing capability-driven setting entities unchanged.

0.4.2-beta7 is cumulative from stable 0.4.1 through beta6; earlier 0.4.2 betas do not need to be installed first.
